quotes.text: Platform security answers, who is allowed to touch this object? Governance of meaning answers, what does this object actually say?
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Separates security from semantic governance in one clean contrast.

quotes.text: Here is the uncomfortable law of large fabric environments. Drift is not a failure. Unobserved drift is.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Reframes drift as something to observe and govern rather than prevent.

quotes.text: What failed was semantic governance and platform boundaries. Self-service without semantic boundaries is not empowerment. It is drift with a friendly UI.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Explains why unrestricted self-service creates shadow analytics.

quotes.text: AI doesn't break your data governance. It removes your ability to hide from how bad it already is. Co-pilot is not a hallucination engine. It is a semantic mirror.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Shows how AI exposes existing semantic debt instead of creating it.

quotes.text: Access control is necessary, it stops the wrong people from touching the right things. Semantic governance is what stops the right people from trusting the wrong things.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: A memorable distinction between access control and governance of meaning.

takeaways: Microsoft Fabric secures objects through Entra, workspace roles, OneLake security and Purview, but it does not govern what metrics and models mean, so semantic drift is guaranteed.
Certified, domain-owned semantic models with named data and semantic owners, domain-aligned workspaces and clear dev, test and prod tiers turn self-service into governed reuse.
Measure consumption on certified models, owner coverage, duplicate KPI definitions, label compliance and AI usage of uncertified models, and constrain Copilot and data agents to certified semantics.
hook: Microsoft Fabric makes it easy to clone semantic models and spin up lakehouses, so organizations end up with several versions of revenue, PHI in the wrong workspace and AI answers grounded on the wrong definitions. This episode is for data leaders, Fabric admins and analytics architects who want a practical governance model with domains, certified semantics, ownership, metrics and a day 0, 30, 90 plan.
